questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: According to the law of demand, what happens to quantity demanded when price rises?

options.text: Quantity demanded increases with higher prices.
Quantity demanded stays the same regardless of price.
Quantity demanded becomes infinite at high prices.

questions.explanation: The law of demand states quantity demanded falls as price rises, holding other factors constant. Rising, constant, or infinite demand are wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Market equilibrium occurs where which two curves intersect?

options.text: Average and marginal cost curves intersect.
Total revenue and total cost curves intersect.
Price ceiling and price floor lines intersect.

questions.explanation: Equilibrium is where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. Cost curves, break-even, and control lines are not market equilibrium.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Name one factor that shifts the demand curve rather than moving along it.

answer.exemplar: Income is a demand shifter: a rise in income shifts demand right for normal goods, while a price change only moves along the curve.

questions.explanation: Income, tastes, expectations, and related prices shift demand; price changes cause movement along it. The wrong idea treats price as a shifter.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Which factor shifts the supply curve?

options.text: A change in consumer income shifts supply.
A change in the good's own price shifts supply.
A change in input prices shifts supply.
A change in quantity demanded shifts supply.

questions.explanation: Input prices, technology, and expectations shift supply. The good's own price causes movement along supply. Income and demand shifts affect demand side.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: When price is above equilibrium, what occurs in the market?

options.text: A shortage, because quantity demanded exceeds supplied.
Equilibrium, because price clears the market.
A surplus, because quantity supplied exceeds demanded.

questions.explanation: Above equilibrium, supply exceeds demand creating a surplus. Shortage, equilibrium, and infinite supply are wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Predict effect of a demand shift
questions.stem: If demand shifts right with supply fixed, what happens to equilibrium price?
questions.explanation: Higher demand with fixed supply raises price. Falling, unchanged, or zero price are wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: What determines how a tax burden is shared between buyers and sellers?

answer.exemplar: Tax incidence depends on relative price elasticities: the side of the market that is less elastic bears the larger share of the tax burden.

questions.explanation: The less elastic side bears more of the tax. The wrong idea is that the side legally paying the tax bears it.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A price floor set above equilibrium causes what?
questions.explanation: A binding price floor above equilibrium creates a surplus. Shortage, no effect, and lower price are wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A price ceiling set below equilibrium causes what?
questions.explanation: A binding price ceiling below equilibrium creates a shortage. Surplus, no effect, and higher price are wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish change in demand from change in quantity demanded
questions.stem: A rise in consumer income for a normal good is what?

options.text: A change in quantity demanded, moving along.
A change in demand, shifting the curve.
A change in supply, shifting supply.

questions.explanation: Income shifts the demand curve. Movement along demand is caused by price changes, not income.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Describe equilibrium adjustment after a shock
questions.stem: After a demand increase, how does the market return to equilibrium?

answer.exemplar: Price rises, reducing quantity demanded and increasing quantity supplied until a new equilibrium with higher price and quantity is reached.

questions.explanation: The price rise rations demand and encourages supply until equality returns. The wrong idea is that quantity adjusts without price change.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: If the price of tea rises, demand for coffee (a substitute) does what?

options.text: Stays the same, as habits fix demand.
Decreases, as consumers buy less of both.

questions.explanation: Substitutes see demand rise when the other good's price rises. Decrease, no change, or zero are wrong.
questions.hint: Substitutes rise together in price effect.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: According to the law of supply, what happens to quantity supplied when price rises?

options.text: Quantity supplied decreases with higher prices.
Quantity supplied is fixed regardless of price.

questions.explanation: The law of supply states quantity supplied rises as price rises. Decrease, fixed, or negative supply are wrong.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute equilibrium price from demand and supply
questions.stem: Demand is Qd equals 10 minus P and supply is Qs equals P minus 2; find equilibrium price.
questions.explanation: Set 10 minus P equal to P minus 2, giving 2P equals 12 and P equals 6. Solving only demand gives 10, which is wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute new equilibrium after demand shift
questions.stem: Demand shifts from Qd equals 10 minus P to Qd equals 14 minus P with Qs equals P minus 2; find new equilibrium price.

answer.exemplar: New equilibrium sets 14 - P = P - 2, so 2P = 16 and P = 8; the price rises from 6 to 8.

questions.explanation: Solving gives P equals 8. Keeping the old price 6 ignores the shift.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute new equilibrium after supply shift
questions.stem: Supply shifts from Qs equals P minus 2 to Qs equals P minus 6 with Qd equals 10 minus P; find new equilibrium price.
questions.explanation: Set 10 minus P equal to P minus 6, giving 2P equals 16 and P equals 8. Using old supply gives 6, which is wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: At price 8 with Qd equals 10 minus P and Qs equals P minus 2, find the surplus.
questions.explanation: At P equals 8, Qs equals 6 and Qd equals 2, so surplus is 4. Reversing, using price, or assuming equilibrium are wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Predict quantity effect of supply shift
questions.stem: If supply shifts right with demand fixed, what happens to equilibrium quantity?
questions.explanation: More supply at each price lowers price and raises quantity. Falling, unchanged, or infinite quantity are wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A tax is imposed; buyers are less elastic than sellers. Who bears more burden?

answer.exemplar: Buyers bear more of the tax burden because the less elastic side cannot adjust quantity easily and so absorbs the price increase.

questions.explanation: The less elastic side bears more. The wrong idea is that the legally assigned side bears it.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute surplus from a price floor
questions.stem: With Qd equals 10 minus P and Qs equals P minus 2, a floor at 9 creates what surplus?
questions.explanation: At P equals 9, Qs equals 7 and Qd equals 1, surplus 6? Wait 7-1=6. Let me set value 6. Explanation: Qs 7 minus Qd 1 equals 6. Using 9 gives 7? I'll correct to 6. Hmm value 6.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute shortage from a price ceiling
questions.stem: With Qd equals 10 minus P and Qs equals P minus 2, a ceiling at 4 creates what shortage?
questions.explanation: At P equals 4, Qd equals 6 and Qs equals 2, shortage 4. Reversing, using price, or no effect are wrong.

provenance.author: bank-team-microeconomics

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Predict effect of income fall on demand
questions.stem: If consumer income falls for a normal good, demand shifts?
questions.explanation: Lower income reduces demand for normal goods, shifting left. Right, no shift, or vertical are wrong.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Describe adjustment to a supply shock
questions.stem: After a supply decrease, how does the market adjust?

answer.exemplar: Price rises and quantity falls until quantity demanded equals the new lower supply, restoring equilibrium at a higher price.

questions.explanation: Price rises to reduce demand and increase supply incentives until equality returns. Quantity alone adjusting is wrong.

questions.explanation: Complements see demand rise when the other good's price falls. Decrease, no change, or zero are wrong.

questions.stem: The phrase ceteris paribus in demand analysis means?

options.text: Income is allowed to vary freely.

questions.explanation: Ceteris paribus holds other factors constant. Price fixed, income varying, or supply-only are wrong.

questions.explanation: Tastes and expectations are demand shifters; technology is a supply shifter. The wrong idea lumps all three as demand shifters.

questions.explanation: Input prices and producer taxes shift supply; income shifts demand. All three or none are wrong.

Infinite demand, because price is cheap.

questions.explanation: Below equilibrium demand exceeds supply causing a shortage. Surplus, equilibrium, and infinite demand are wrong.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Compute price effect of a tax
questions.stem: A per-unit tax is imposed; how does it affect equilibrium price and quantity?

answer.exemplar: The tax shifts supply left, raising equilibrium price and lowering equilibrium quantity.

questions.explanation: The tax increases marginal cost, shifting supply left, so price rises and quantity falls. The wrong idea is that only quantity changes.

questions.learningObjective: Identify when a price ceiling is non-binding

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: If demand and supply both increase, what is certain about equilibrium quantity?

answer.exemplar: Equilibrium quantity definitely rises, because both shifts push quantity up, though the price change is ambiguous.

questions.explanation: Both shifts raise quantity, so quantity rises. Price may rise or fall depending on relative shifts. The wrong idea is that both price and quantity are ambiguous.
